messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD GPU queue length > 2000 (us-west-2) — autoscaler failing to add nodes. Alert ID: alert-ptn-2319. Link: https://monitoring.internal/redwood/alerts/alert-ptn-2319

sasha: ack, I'm on it. seeing sustained enqueue rate from /generate and /chat routes. latency spiking (p50 380ms -> p50 1.6s).

mike: what failure are we seeing from the cluster-autoscaler? logs?

cheng: copying relevant CA logs from node-autoscaler: 
```
I0321 14:02:12.123456 1 scale_up.go:341] Pod xyz pending for 22s: insufficient gpu
E0321 14:02:13.234567 1 aws_manager.go:512] error describing launch template versions: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation
	status code: 403, request id: arn:aws:ec2:us-west-2:xxx:launch-template/lt-0abcd
E0321 14:02:14.345678 1 scale_up.go:412] scale-up failed: launch template drift detected, skipping nodegroup create
```

sasha: so CA can't create ASG/node group due to launch template API 403. we had a rollout that updated LT last night; possible iam role change?

jordana: paging infra-iam: @kevin can you confirm the instance-profile/role the autoscaler uses has ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions?

kevin: looking. the role used by autoscaler is infra-autoscaler-role. recent policy patch removed ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions (it was scoped during lockdown). rolling it back now. ETA 3m.

support-bot: Noted: customer-impact tag added to alert (customers: several Dedicated clusters experiencing high retries).

mike: while kevin is rolling policy, we need short-term mitigation: CA will keep failing. can we manually scale a spare GPU nodegroup? any spare capacity?

cheng: we have a warm pool gm-gpu-warm in us-west-2 but it currently has taints: workload=isolated:NoSchedule (used for dedicated). If we untaint temporarily, it can accept requests. proposal: add nodegroup with launch-template-version 7 (previous working), or untaint warm nodes and mount our kube labels.

sasha: risk check: untainting might let dedicated tenants land there — we must ensure network/tenant isolation isn't violated. but as emergency we can reassign capacity to system pool and throttle non-critical customers.

jordana: support team, start notifying largest affected customers and switch any pre-scheduled background batch jobs to the low-priority queue.

pd-oncall: I have the PD. setting Sev 2. escalate if we can't restore autoscaling in 15m.

kevin: policy roll-back applied. I can run a quick call to verify permissions:
```
> aws iam simulate-principal-policy --policy-source-arn arn:aws:iam::123:role/infra-autoscaler-role --action-names ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions
{"IsAllowed": true}
```

mike: good. can we trigger a manual CA reconcile?

cheng: doing a CA pod restart to pick up new creds and force scale attempt. /pods/cluster-autoscaler restart in kube-system.

incident-bot: deploy-bot: cluster-autoscaler restart triggered by cheng at 14:07:22 UTC.

sasha: CA logs after restart show a different failure: 
```
I0321 14:08:05.789012 1 aws_manager.go:458] LaunchTemplateVersion 7 found for lt-0abcd
E0321 14:08:06.890123 1 asg.go:621] error creating asg: you must specify at least one subnet for launch template, InvalidParameter: SubnetIds not provided
```

mike: hmm launch template version 7 is missing subnet override the new config expects. that explains the 'drift' message earlier. seems like a new cluster provisioning workflow changed required fields.

jordana: action items: 1) manually create nodegroup with corrected launch template + subnet ids, 2) temporarily untaint warm pool as backup, 3) throttle low-priority traffic and fallback to smaller models for best-effort customers. who owns (1)?

cheng: I can create the nodegroup manually via console/terraform: create ASG using LT version 8 with subnet list [subnet-aaa, subnet-bbb], instance type p4d.24xlarge. doing a quick create now.

sasha: meanwhile, enable per-route throttles: set /generate rate-limit to 60r/s (was 200r/s) for non-paid tiers. push config to api-gateway: `curl -X POST https://ops.internal/config/throttle -d '{"route":"/generate","limit":60}'`

support-bot: mass DM sent to support channel with templated customer message: "We're experiencing degraded performance for generation requests in us-west-2. Engineers are actively mitigating. No data loss. We'll update in 30m."

kevin: new nodegroup create returned: ASG created, instances launching. Cloud reports instances passing healthchecks 14:12:03 -> nodes join k8s 14:13:10.

mike: CA now recognizes extra capacity and starts issuing binding events. queue depth falling: 1950 -> 600 in 8m. nice.

sasha: still seeing a small proportion of pods failing scheduling due to taints on some nodes: we should cordon dedicated-only nodes and label the new nodes with pool=shared.

cheng: applied label pool=shared to new nodes and removed NoSchedule taint on warm pool temporarily.

incident-bot: monitoring update: queue length 600, p50 480ms, p95 2.1s.

jordana: support: share a brief update to customers: "We've brought additional GPU capacity online and reduced queue; you may see retries for a few minutes. We expect full recovery within 30 minutes."

pd-oncall: handing off oncall to cheng for overnight watch. pd-oncall will stay available for escalation.

cheng: I'll watch autoscaler metrics and node join events. if we see another launch-template/version mismatch, escalate to infra-allocations to freeze any LT changes.

sasha: quick root-cause notes in thread: recent infra lockdown changed IAM policy for autoscaler removing DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions -> CA failed 403 -> CA attempted but LT versions mismatched (missing subnet override) -> CA skipped scale up -> queue growth -> manual nodegroup creation & untainting warm pool as stopgap.

mike: remediation tasks (tracked in #infra-ops board): 1) restore IAM least-privilege with explicit ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions on infra-autoscaler-role, 2) add automated LT schema validation during LT updates, 3) add a warm-pool fallback runbook to avoid manual untainting, 4) update runbooks to throttle non-critical tenants automatically on queue signals.

jordana: assigning follow-ups to infra and runtime teams. will open a postmortem request and schedule incident review.

sasha: thanks everyone. I'll update the incident ticket and close the pager once queue stays < 100 for 20m. :white_check_mark:
